text.p: The Washington Post carried the following items on the front page of its business section on Sept. 25:

WASHINGTON - AT&T Corp. Chairman Robert Allen announced that third and fourth quarter earnings would fall below analysts' expectations due largely to consumer defections from its long-distance service.
WASHINGTON - Robert Johnson, founder of the Black Entertainment Network, announced plans for the nation's first African American movie channel.
WASHINGTON - Best Products Co., citing sagging sales and a deterioration of vendor support, filed for federal bankruptcy protection in Richmond, Va.
WASHINGTON - Thousands of government officials, financiers, activists and journalists from around the world are converging on the capital this week for the annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank.
